questions.stem: The firefighters worked through the night to put ___ the fire.
questions.explanation: 'Put out' a fire means to stop it burning.

distractors.D: 'put down' means place on a surface

questions.stem: Please ___ attention while I explain the rules.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'pay attention'.

distractors.D: you give a speech, not attention (in this phrase)

questions.stem: Mia was so tired that she fell ___ asleep on the couch.
questions.explanation: 'Fast asleep' means sleeping deeply.

distractors.D: you can be in a deep sleep, but not 'deep asleep'

questions.stem: Can you ___ me a favour and hold the door?
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'do someone a favour'.

distractors.A: you make a mistake, not a favour
distractors.C: 'give a favour' isn't the usual phrase

questions.stem: The old bridge was too ___ for the heavy truck to cross.
questions.explanation: A bridge that can't hold a heavy load is weak.

distractors.C: describes how something feels to touch

questions.stem: We waited in a long ___ to buy tickets for the show.
questions.explanation: People waiting one behind another stand in a queue.

distractors.C: a group isn't waiting in order
distractors.A: a crowd is a mass of people, not a line
distractors.D: a team works or plays together

questions.stem: It started to rain, so we ran for ___ under a tree.
questions.explanation: You 'run for shelter' to get out of the rain.

distractors.B: a net that catches you if you fall

questions.stem: The puppy was so ___ that it chewed every shoe in the house.
questions.explanation: Chewing every shoe is naughty behaviour.

distractors.D: the opposite of what the puppy did

questions.stem: Dad asked me to ___ the table before dinner.
questions.explanation: 'Set the table' means put out plates and cutlery.

distractors.A: you put things on the table, but not 'put the table'
distractors.D: you make a bed, not a table (for dinner)

questions.stem: The athlete broke the world ___ for the 100-metre race.
questions.explanation: You 'break a record' by doing better than anyone before.

questions.stem: Ella took a deep ___ before she jumped into the cold water.
questions.explanation: 'Breath' is the noun: take a deep breath.

questions.stem: The magician made the rabbit ___ into thin air.
questions.explanation: 'Disappear into thin air' means vanish completely.

distractors.A: means not do as you are told

questions.stem: Our team was ___ when we lost the final by one point.
questions.explanation: Losing by one point would make you disappointed.

distractors.C: means glad something bad is over

questions.stem: The teacher asked us to work ___ pairs.
questions.explanation: We say 'work in pairs'.

questions.stem: The glass slipped out of my hand and ___ into pieces.
questions.explanation: Glass smashes into pieces.

questions.stem: A spider spun a ___ in the corner of the window.
questions.explanation: Spiders spin webs.

questions.stem: You need to ___ your teeth twice a day.
questions.explanation: We brush our teeth.

questions.stem: The sun ___ in the east every morning.
questions.explanation: The sun 'rises' (it goes up by itself).

distractors.A: 'raise' needs an object: you raise your hand
distractors.B: people climb; we don't say the sun climbs up

questions.stem: She is very ___ at drawing animals.
questions.explanation: We say 'good at' something.

distractors.D: 'well' is an adverb: she draws well

questions.stem: The car ran ___ of petrol on the way home.
questions.explanation: 'Run out of' means have none left.

distractors.B: 'run over' means hit with a car

questions.stem: The baby ___ loudly when she dropped her toy.
questions.explanation: A baby who drops a toy is likely to cry loudly.

questions.stem: We could hear the ___ of the waves on the rocks.
questions.explanation: Waves crash on rocks.

questions.stem: Tom made a ___ when he spelled 'friend' as 'freind'.
questions.explanation: We 'make a mistake'.

distractors.D: 'make a problem' isn't the usual phrase

questions.stem: The movie was so ___ that I watched it three times.
questions.explanation: If you watch it three times, it was enjoyable.

distractors.A: describes a person, not a movie
